title: Local Emulation & Telemetry Harness for SDKs (Quickstart)
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Overview

This guide describes a lightweight, reproducible local emulation and telemetry harness for Redwood SDKs. The harness is intended for SDK authors and integration engineers to:

- run deterministic unit and integration tests against a local stub of the Redwood API;
- capture and assert telemetry/metrics emitted by SDKs (latency, token counts, errors);
- record stable golden responses for offline CI and flakey-network simulation;
- exercise fallback and retry logic without incurring hosted costs.

Audience and objectives

- Audience: SDK authors, developer-experience engineers, QA engineers working on client libraries.
- Objectives: Provide a canonical local testbed with documented commands, example configs, and canonical fixes for top support issues related to local development and telemetry.

When to use this harness

Use the local emulation harness when:

1. You need deterministic unit tests for prompting logic or streaming behavior.
2. You want to validate SDK telemetry (events and metrics) before releasing.
3. You need to validate fallback behavior (e.g., model variant fallback, local cache hit/miss) under controlled conditions.

Quickstart (5 minutes)

Prereqs: Docker, Node 18+ (or Python 3.10+ for python-sdk tests), Make, jq.

1) Clone the devx harness repo (internal):

   git clone git@redwood.company:devx/sdk-emulation-harness.git && cd sdk-emulation-harness

2) Start the local stub and telemetry backend:

   make up

   This runs three containers: 
   - redwood-stub: HTTP/HTTP2 stub replicating Redwood API surface (generation, embeddings, streaming).
   - telemetry-collector: prometheus-compatible pushgateway + local event sink.
   - proxy-router: optional local routing layer that simulates latency/failures.

3) Configure your SDK to point at the stub (example env vars):

   export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=test_local_key
   export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_URL=http://localhost:9091/events

4) Run the sample Node.js quicktest:

   cd examples/node && npm ci && npm test

Expected outcome: tests pass, telemetry events appear at http://localhost:9091/ui and metrics at http://localhost:9091/metrics

Configuration reference (table)

| Variable | Default | Description | Accepts |
| REDWOOD_API_URL | http://localhost:8080 | Base URL for API requests | http(s) URL |
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | test_local_key | API key accepted by stub (non-prod) | string |
| REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_URL | http://localhost:9091/events | Event sink for SDKs to POST structured telemetry | http(s) URL |
| STUB_LATENCY_MS | 0 | Inject uniform request latency for simulation | integer (ms) |
| RECORD_RESPONSES | false | When true, stub will persist responses to /recordings | true/false |

Example SDK config (node-style JSON)

{
  "client": {
    "baseUrl": "http://localhost:8080",
    "apiKey": "test_local_key",
    "timeoutMs": 180000,
    "telemetryEndpoint": "http://localhost:9091/events"
  },
  "retry": {
    "maxAttempts": 3,
    "initialBackoffMs": 50,
    "maxBackoffMs": 1000
  },
  "telemetry": {
    "emitTokenCount": true,
    "emitLatencyMs": true,
    "batchIntervalMs": 500
  }
}

Golden recordings and offline CI

- To enable golden recordings set RECORD_RESPONSES=true and run the e2e recording job:

  make record-suite SUITE=generator-basic

- Recordings are stored under harness/recordings/<suite-name>/<sha>.json and are checked into an internal artifacts bucket.
- CI job (recording-disabled) will replay recordings using the stub's --replay-mode to ensure test determinism.

Telemetry contract and assertions

Telemetry from SDKs follows a compact JSON event schema (excerpt):

{
  "event_type": "sdk.request",
  "sdk_name": "redwood-js",
  "sdk_version": "0.23.1",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "duration_ms": 34,
  "tokens_in": 12,
  "tokens_out": 56,
  "status": "ok"
}

Recommended assertions for CI:

- Every request must emit an sdk.request event within 1s of completion.
- Duration_ms must be < 5000ms for unit tests (can be relaxed in integration staging).
- Token counts must be non-negative integers and match snapshot ranges for the prompt set.

Common test suites included

1. generator-basic: simple generation, no streaming.
2. stream-echo: streaming chunk handling with backpressure tests.
3. embed-equality: embeddings for canonical inputs, tolerance 1e-6.
4. fallback-flow: primary model fails with 500, fallback to variant2 succeeds.
5. offline-golden-replay: replay previously recorded responses and assert SDK outputs.

Rollout checklist for SDK authors

1. Add harness integration to PR checks (+1 reviewer from devx).
2. Add telemetry assertions for new API paths (see Telemetry contract).
3. Run make record-suite locally and commit any new golden recordings to the artifacts bucket (not to git).
4. Update CHANGELOG with testing coverage notes.

Ownership and SLAs

- Owners: devx/sdk-integration (primary), devx-observability (telemetry collector).
- Support SLA for the harness: 3 business days for triage (devx team).

Troubleshooting & canonical fixes (top support issues)

1) Symptom: SDK tests fail with connection refused to localhost:8080
   Cause: Stub didn't start or Docker port conflict.
   Fix: run docker ps | rg sdk-emulation; docker-compose logs redwood-stub; increase Docker resources and retry make up.

2) Symptom: Telemetry events not visible in UI
   Cause: SDK misconfigured telemetry endpoint or CORS blocking in browser UI.
   Fix: verify REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_URL, curl the endpoint: curl -v -XPOST http://localhost:9091/events -d '{"test":1}' and check collector logs. If UI blocked, open collector UI on 9091 (no-auth in dev).

3) Symptom: Streaming tests hang intermittently
   Cause: Proxy-router injecting large latency or stub stuck buffering.
   Fix: disable proxy latency (STUB_LATENCY_MS=0), restart stub, and run stream-echo with verbose logging. Increase stream timeouts in tests to 30s for CI.

4) Symptom: Golden replay mismatch (hash differs)
   Cause: Non-deterministic fields in response (timestamp, request_id) were not scrubbed.
   Fix: Use the scrubbing filter in harness/scripts/scrub-recording.js; re-record with SCRUB=true.

5) Symptom: CI flakes with token-count mismatch
   Cause: Tokenization differences between SDK and recording environment.
   Fix: pin tokenizer version in test env or run recorder with the same tokenizer container (see embeddings/README).

Templates and example snippets

- CI job snippet (GitHub Actions):

  jobs:
    sdk-test:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - name: Start harness
          run: docker-compose -f harness/docker-compose.ci.yml up -d --build
        - name: Run tests
          run: make ci-test SUITE=generator-basic

- Node usage example (snippet):

  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_API_URL, apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-base-1', input: 'Hello' });

Appendix: Scripts and helpers

- make up/down/status — manage local containers.
- make record-suite SUITE=<name> — run and persist recordings.
- harness/scripts/scrub-recording.js — scrub request_id, timestamps, variable fields.
- harness/telemetry/assertions/ — JSON assertion templates used by CI.
